text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Hackers broke into the internet page of Poland's prime minister and changed its content. The page was not linked with the government's software database and hackers could not access it, cabinet spokesperson Aleksandra Jakubowska said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The Plus GSM digital mobile phone operator has signed a roaming agreement with Britain's DCS 1800 Orange system, Plus GSM said.
- Over 100 Polish and international forestry firms will exhibit their equipment and technologies at the Fourth International Forestry Fair in Warsaw to start on May 13.

- Daewoo FSO will buy the Pultusk branch of the Warszawska Fabryka Platerow (WFP) silverware plant from WFP, which is controlled by the Universal capital group. South Korean-owned Daewoo FSO plans to make car accessories at the Pultusk plant.
- The listed Swarzedzkie Fabryki Mebli furniture maker's sales will exceed 170 million zlotys this year, showing a 60 percent upturn compared with 1996, the company's forecast said.
- Pentrator brokerage house in Krakow will open its first outlet in Warsaw in mid-May, Penetrator's president Andrzej Madej said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- If the purchase of Polish Investment Bank (PBI) by Kredyt Bank is declared void, Creditanstalt will again offer to buy PBI, Creditanstalt Financial Advisers Director Richard Golden said.
- Poland's exports to Turkey were worth $57.4 million in 1996 and the value of imports was $92.8 million, showing a trade deficit of $35.4 million.
- Poland's furniture exports exceeded $1.5 billion in 1996 with 76 percent sold on the EU markets.
- Out of 75 daily newspapers published in Poland in 1988, only 20 are still in circulation.

- Zaklady Naprawcze Taboru Kolejowego (ZNTK) rolling stock maintenance firm made a net profit of 1.6 million zlotys last year but the value of sales was over 6.0 million zlotys lower than forecast initially, the company said.

- Polish coffee consumers favour natural ground coffee which accounts for the biggest sales, instant coffee comes second and coffee beans third, according to a report by the Indicator market research agency. Only one in 15 Poles drinks decaffeinated coffee.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The listed Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy Bank (WBK), controlled by Allied Irish Banks (AIB), will launch a new VISA Electron credit card addressed to low income customers, the bank's spokesperson Marek Szczepanski said.
ZYCIE

- The IBM Poland, JTT and Optimus computer hardware makers will start marketing computers equipped with Pentium-2 processors this week. The new computers will be priced between 8,500 and 9,600 zlotys.
PARKIET
- The KGHM copper combine has presented the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) with a share issue prospectus. The company plans to sell shares in June, KGHM's spokesperson Piotr Bielawski said.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
